Shrink regression coefficients towards zero

Source: R/priors-regularized.R
prior_regularized.Rd

Shrink continuous slopes and factor effects using ridge, lasso or horseshoe priors. The fitted contrast determines which coefficients shrink together. All members of a named group share the global scale and, when specified, the slab variance.

prior_regularized(
  family,
  scale,
  terms = NULL,
  slab_scale = NULL,
  slab_df = 4,
  contrast = NULL
)

Arguments

family

One of "ridge", "lasso", and "horseshoe".

scale

A positive number fixing the global scale, or a proper scalar continuous prior with positive support from which to learn it. The scale is in fitted coefficient units. For a single lasso coefficient it is the Laplace scale. For a centered factor it scales the Euclidean norm in the group-lasso density.

terms

Optional character vector of fixed-effect term labels. Place a group under its own name in the formula prior list. Omitting terms selects the non-intercept terms without a prior of their own. Separate named groups have independent scales, even if they use the same scale prior. A multi-column term uses its fitted coefficient basis.

slab_scale

Positive scale of the Student-t slab for the regularized horseshoe. The default NULL selects the classical horseshoe.

slab_df

Positive degrees of freedom of the Student-t slab.

contrast

Optional factor coding, one of "treatment", "independent", "meandif" or "orthonormal". With NULL, JAGS_formula() uses treatment coding by default and a calling model can supply its factor coding.

Value

With numeric scale and omitted terms, ridge and lasso return ordinary scalar priors accepted by prior_spike_and_slab() and prior_mixture(). Otherwise the result declares a coefficient group for JAGS_formula(). is.prior.regularized() identifies group declarations. is.prior.regularized_term() identifies coefficient priors bound to a group.

Details

A continuous slope is one shrinkage unit. Treatment coding gives one unit per difference from the reference level. Independent coding gives one per level coefficient. Mean-difference and orthonormal coding place the centered coefficients of a factor in one exchangeable unit. In an interaction the fitted codings of the constituent factors determine the units. Centered factors form one unit per column combination of partners coded by treatment contrasts or level indicators. A group that supplies a factor main effect can use its requested contrast for that factor while a separately specified partner retains its own coding. If the group supplies only the interaction, an explicit contrast must match the fitted coding of every constituent that uses a contrast. Omit contrast to inherit a mixed design. Formula-forced level indicators keep their indicator coding.

For a unit of dimension \(d\), write \(b\) for its vector of coded coefficients and \(\tau\) for the global scale. Ridge gives \(b\) a spherical Normal prior with coordinate standard deviation \(\tau\). Group lasso has density proportional to \(\tau^{-d}\exp(-\|b\|_2/\tau)\). Equivalently, conditional on one variance multiplier \(W\) with Gamma shape \((d+1)/2\) and rate \(1/2\), its coordinates are independent Normals with standard deviation \(\tau\sqrt{W}\) (Kyung et al. 2010) . Each coordinate has variance \((d+1)\tau^2\) given \(\tau\). A one-dimensional unit has the ordinary Laplace distribution with scale \(\tau\).

The horseshoe draws one standard half-Cauchy local scale per unit. Conditional on global scale \(\tau\) and its unit's local scale \(\lambda_j\), a horseshoe coefficient is Normal with mean zero and standard deviation \(s_j = \tau\lambda_j\). With a finite slab its conditional variance is \(c^2 s_j^2/(c^2+s_j^2)\), where the shared \(c^2\) follows an inverse-gamma distribution with shape \(\nu/2\) and scale \(\nu s^2/2\) for \(\nu=\) slab_df and \(s=\) slab_scale (Piironen and Vehtari 2017) .

Both centered codings give exchangeable level deviations. They retain the scale convention of prior_factor(). For a main effect with \(K\) levels the mean-difference contrast matrix is the orthonormal contrast matrix divided by \(\sqrt{1-1/K}\). Thus the same coded scale gives larger level deviations under mean-difference coding.

The horseshoe has a continuous density with an infinite peak at zero, including with a finite slab. A point hypothesis at zero cannot use the Savage-Dickey density ratio. Use explicit point-null models for inclusion probabilities. Prior draws within a group retain its common scales when forming contrasts. Where an analytic contrast distribution is unavailable, the joint prior draws can still be used. Density and probability calculations for a contrast of two coordinate-wise lasso coefficients sharing a learned scale integrate its conditional convolution over that scale. Within one centered unit, a linear contrast has the marginal law of one coded coordinate scaled by the Euclidean length of its weight vector. For wider coordinate-wise shared-lasso contrasts, plots omit unresolved prior curves. For a bound centered factor, the marginal methods such as mpdf() describe a level deviation using the fitted contrast matrix. Use JAGS_formula_prior_density() for a particular coefficient or contrast, and rng() for joint draws. For terms with several coefficients, a joint density, CDF or quantile request raises BayesTools_regularized_joint_unavailable. A marginal calculation that cannot meet its numerical precision raises BayesTools_regularized_marginal_unavailable.

References

Kyung M, Gill J, Ghosh M, Casella G (2010). “Penalized regression, standard errors, and Bayesian lassos.” Bayesian Analysis, 5(2), 369–412. doi:10.1214/10-BA607 .

Piironen J, Vehtari A (2017). “Sparsity information and regularization in the horseshoe and other shrinkage priors.” Electronic Journal of Statistics, 11(2). doi:10.1214/17-EJS1337SI .

Examples

prior_regularized("ridge", scale = 0.5)
#> Normal(0, 0.5)
prior_regularized("lasso", scale = 0.5)
#> Laplace(0, 0.5)
global <- prior("cauchy", list(0, 0.2), truncation = list(0, Inf))
intercept <- prior("normal", list(0, 2))
# All slopes share a global scale.
all_slopes <- list(intercept = intercept, sh = prior_regularized("horseshoe", global))
# Only wt and hp share shrinkage; disp has its own Normal prior.
priors <- list(
  intercept = intercept, disp = prior("normal", list(0, 0.5)),
  shrinkage = prior_regularized("horseshoe", scale = global,
                                terms = c("wt", "hp"), slab_scale = 2)
)
JAGS_formula(~ wt + hp + disp, "mu", mtcars, prior_list = priors)

# Two groups give wt and hp independent global scales.
separate <- list(intercept = intercept,
                 sh_wt = prior_regularized("horseshoe", global, terms = "wt"),
                 sh_hp = prior_regularized("horseshoe", global, terms = "hp"))
# One global scale for Wind and Month. Month has one local horseshoe
# scale for all four of its centered coordinates. Wind has its own.
weather <- transform(airquality, Month = factor(Month))
group <- prior_regularized("horseshoe", global, terms = c("Month", "Wind"),
                           contrast = "meandif")
centered <- JAGS_formula(~ Month + Wind, "mu", weather,
                         prior_list = list(intercept = intercept, sh = group))
# Group lasso on the orthonormal month coordinates.
month_lasso <- prior_regularized("lasso", global, terms = "Month",
                                 contrast = "orthonormal")
